identity: The complete lower 1897 row is assigned to seven point. Compared with ten point, T is about 6–10% wider while U is about 8–9% narrower at threshold 205 in both 1897 and document specimens. Compared with eight point, T/U are about 5–7% wider in both specimens. Opposing differences within a row rule out uniform scan stretch. Figure proportions also distinguish the six-point cut.
visual_review: All 37 visible native crops and final silhouettes reviewed at 185 and 32 pixels; words reviewed at 16/24/40/64/96 pixels. Four final trial sheets, seven threshold sheets and all native identity comparisons inspected. The J hook, figure 7 arm and both figure 8 bowls are complete. The full 36-character comparison with the canonical twelve-point cut was inspected.
source_choices: All capitals and figures use the lower alphabet under the shared 1897 six/seven-point heading, assigned to seven point using the separately labelled document specimen and native cap-height ratios. The period is doc7-34. Four source books are retained, with two supplying traced forms.
rejected_trials: The initial capital threshold 190 and figure threshold 215 included excess scan fringe. Most capitals retain their complete native form at 175; G/Q use 185, J uses 195 and Z uses 205.
Lower thresholds lose the J hook, figure 3 top, figure 4 arm, figure 7 stem and figure 8/9 bowl joins. Individual thresholds 175–205 retain the complete observed forms.
geometry: Uniform measured cap scale and rigid source-row rotation. The separate figure group uses its own local baseline measured from 1/4/7 at the same physical scale. No independent width fitting, hole filling or drawn replacement strokes.
native_limitations: Minor print irregularities, including angularity in the small figure 3 and figure 4 arm, remain visible in the selected native impressions. These have not been replaced by idealized drawings.
